name: Lindner Präzisionsguss GmbH
industry: Aluminium high-pressure die casting for e-mobility structural parts
description: Lindner Präzisionsguss GmbH is a family-owned die caster with 320 employees that produces thin-walled aluminium structural parts for electric vehicles: shock towers, battery-housing frames, longitudinal members and cross-car beams for German and European OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. It runs eight cold-chamber high-pressure die casting cells between 2,500 and 4,400 tonnes, in-house heat treatment, CNC finishing and X-ray inspection. Its competitive edge is tight dimensional tolerance and fast ramp-up of new parts; its main risks are OEMs moving to in-house gigacasting, rising CO2 requirements on aluminium, and energy costs.

watch_fields.name: Gigacasting / mega-casting
watch_fields.description: Very large single-piece structural castings made on 6,000 to 16,000 tonne presses. Threat if OEMs insource body structures; opportunity if Lindner can supply mid-size integrated castings or tooling know-how.

watch_fields.name: Recycled & low-carbon aluminium alloys
watch_fields.description: Secondary and low-CO2 aluminium, scrap-tolerant and non-heat-treatable alloys for structural castings, plus the price and carbon rules (CBAM, PCF) that shape demand.

watch_fields.name: AI-based casting defect detection
watch_fields.description: Machine learning on X-ray, CT and camera images to find porosity, cracks and cold shuts automatically, inline and at cycle time.

watch_fields.name: Digital twins & simulation for die casting
watch_fields.description: Casting process simulation, solidification and die-thermal models, and plant-level digital twins that cut tool trials and scrap during ramp-up.
